input.question: besides the dollar amount, what the hell are autioneers actually saying?
input.ground_truth: It doesn't really matter what they're saying. The point is to get you psyched up and excited so you're more prone to buying something. All about energy levels moreso than actual content. If you go to some auctions for more expensive items (luxury cars, art, etc.), then you'll probably hear a slower auctioneer and a more thorough description of the item.

Okay! Imagine you and your friend are playing a game where you both want the same toy. An auctioneer is like a helper who helps you and your friend decide who gets the toy. But instead of just saying “You get it!” or “You get it!”, the auctioneer says a bunch of fast words that sound like a secret code.

Here’s what the auctioneer is really saying:

- “Do I hear any more money?” (Are you or anyone else going to pay more for the toy?)
- “It’s going for…” (This is the new price. Someone just agreed to pay this much.)
- “Sold!” (Someone has agreed to pay the most, and now the toy is theirs.)

So, besides saying how much money, the auctioneer is asking if anyone else wants the toy more and telling everyone when someone wins. It’s like a game of “Who wants it more and is willing to pay more?”
